title: Mobutu Sese Seko | The King of the Kleptocrats
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，你好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在这里，你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上稀奇古怪、美妙绝伦的事物，同时提升你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today is the start of yet another three-part mini-series, this time on the loose theme of “power struggles in post-colonial Africa”.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们开始一个新的三集迷你系列，这次的主题大致是“后殖民时期非洲的权力斗争”。

sentences.en: In part one, today’s episode, we are going to learn about Mobutu Sese Seko, the man who ruled the Democratic Republic of Congo with an iron fist and a leopard-skin hat.
sentences.zh: 在今天的第一集里，我们将了解 Mobutu Sese Seko，这个用铁腕和豹皮帽统治刚果民主共和国的男人。

sentences.en: In part two, we are going to learn about the curious case of the man who went to Eton, the most exclusive private school in Britain, studying alongside princes and plutocrats, but was arrested on the charge of attempting a military coup in Equatorial Guinea.
sentences.zh: 在第二集中，我们将了解一个离奇的案件：一个曾在英国最顶尖的私立学校伊顿公学与王子和富豪们一同求学的男子，却因企图在赤道几内亚发动军事政变而被捕。

sentences.en: And in part three, we are going to zoom in on Angola to understand how Chinese power and money have changed the rules of the game in post-colonial Africa.
sentences.zh: 在第三集中，我们将聚焦安哥拉，了解中国权力和资金如何改变了后殖民非洲的游戏规则。

sentences.en: Ok then, let’s get right into it and talk about Mobutu Sese Seko.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们这就切入正题，聊聊 Mobutu Sese Seko。

sentences.en: There was a 1990 New York Times bestseller called A Natural History of the Senses, where the author went into detail about the reasons that tastes change over time.
sentences.zh: 1990年曾有一本畅销书叫《感官自然史》（A Natural History of the Senses），书中详细探讨了人的口味随时间改变的原因。

sentences.en: Why do children tend to dislike certain flavours but start to enjoy them as young adults?
sentences.zh: 为什么孩子们往往讨厌某些味道，但在青年时期却开始喜欢它们？

sentences.en: Why are our preferences at 45 often different from those at 25?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们在45岁时的偏好常常与25岁时不同？

sentences.en: In the case of today’s protagonist, at the age of 25, his favourite drink–and his only contribution to his wedding banquet –was a single crate of beer, but at 45, his tastes had evolved.
sentences.zh: 对于今天的主人公来说，在25岁时，他最喜欢的饮料——也是他为婚宴准备的唯一贡品——只是一箱啤酒，但到了45岁，他的品味已经升级了。

sentences.en: Any guest at one of his parties would be greeted with a flute of Pink Laurent Perrier champagne.
sentences.zh: 任何参加他派对的客人都将受到一杯粉红罗兰百瑞香槟的迎接。

sentences.en: Now, this is probably not best explained by any scientific theory, but rather by the fact that at 25, he was a lowly army officer, and at 45, he was the undisputed leader of sub-Saharan Africa’s largest country, and by some estimates, one of the wealthiest men in the world.
sentences.zh: 这可能很难用什么科学理论来解释，倒不如说是因为：25岁时，他只是一名卑微的陆军军官；而45岁时，他已经是撒哈拉以南非洲最大国家的无可争议的领导人，据估计，他也是世界上最富有的人之一。

sentences.en: This is the story of Joseph-Désiré Mobutu, or Mobutu Sese Seko, as he would later be called.
sentences.zh: 这就是约瑟夫-德西雷·蒙博托（Joseph-Désiré Mobutu）的故事，也就是后来被称为的 Mobutu Sese Seko。

sentences.en: He was born in 1930, in Lisala, a small town in what was then the Belgian Congo.
sentences.zh: 他于1930年出生在利萨拉（Lisala），这是当时比属刚果的一个小镇。

sentences.en: His mother was a hotel maid, and his father a cook working for a Belgian judge.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲是一名酒店女佣，父亲是为比利时法官工作的厨师。

sentences.en: His father died when he was only 8 years old, and his uncle and grandfather stepped up as sort of joint father figures.
sentences.zh: 在他仅8岁时父亲就去世了，他的叔叔和外祖父充当了某种共同的父亲角色。

sentences.en: It wasn’t a privileged upbringing by any means, but the young boy was clever, confident, and somewhat rebellious.
sentences.zh: 他的成长环境绝对谈不上优越，但这个小男孩聪明、自信，而且有点叛逆。

sentences.en: He was known for all sorts of pranks, tricks on his Catholic school teachers, and with age, these turned from classroom jokes into more serious acts of disobedience.
sentences.zh: 他以各种恶作剧闻名，捉弄天主教学校的老师，随着年龄的增长，这些课堂上的玩笑演变成了更严重的违纪行为。

sentences.en: He even ran away from school on a boat, reportedly to go and meet a girl, and was found downriver several weeks later.
sentences.zh: 他甚至曾坐船逃学，据说为了去见一个女孩，几周后才在下游被找到。

sentences.en: As a punishment for his misbehaviour, he was kicked out of school and forced to join the Force Publique, the colonial army run by the Belgians, where he served for a few years before becoming a journalist.
sentences.zh: 作为对他的惩罚，他被学校开除，被迫加入了由比利时人管理的殖民军队——国民军（Force Publique），他在那里服役几年后成为了一名记者。

sentences.en: Now, before we move on, it’s worth just reminding ourselves a little bit about the history of Congo at the time Mobutu was a young man.
sentences.zh: 在我们继续之前，有必要先回顾一下蒙博托年轻时刚果的历史。

sentences.en: It was a Belgian colony, and of all the colonial regimes in Africa, it 's hard to find one more extractive, oppressive and brutal than the Belgians’ colonisation of the Congo.
sentences.zh: 这里曾是比利时的殖民地，在非洲所有的殖民政权中，很难找到比比利时对刚果的殖民统治更具掠夺性、压迫性和残暴的了。

sentences.en: You might know this already, perhaps you might remember some of this from Episode 289 on King Leopold II, but if you don’t, here’s a brief reminder.
sentences.zh: 你可能已经知道了，也许你还记得第289期关于利奥波德二世国王（King Leopold II）的内容，但如果你不知道，这里有一个简短的回忆。

sentences.en: The country was treated as a vast resource mine— rubber, copper, uranium, diamonds—all extracted for Belgian profit, with practically zero consideration for the livelihood or well-being of any of the native people.
sentences.zh: 这个国家被当作一个巨大的资源矿——橡胶、铜、铀、钻石——全部为比利时的利益而被疯狂掠夺，几乎完全不考虑任何当地人的生计或福祉。

sentences.en: The colonial administrators were fiendishly cruel, and the local population was kept in a state of dependency and fear.
sentences.zh: 殖民地官员极其残酷，当地民众一直生活在依附和恐惧之中。

sentences.en: It was seriously grim, and an estimated 10 million Congolese people were killed directly and indirectly in the first 23 years of Belgian colonisation alone.
sentences.zh: 这极其残酷，据估计，仅在比利时殖民统治的前23年里，就有大约1000万刚果人直接或间接丧生。

sentences.en: And, as per most countries that were colonised, but even more so in the case of Congo, there had been practically no investment in local infrastructure, training of local people, or creation of laws or institutions.
sentences.zh: 而且，就像大多数被殖民的国家一样，刚果的情况更是有过之而无不及，当地几乎没有对基础设施、本地人员培训或法律与机构建设进行任何投资。

sentences.en: This meant that when independence came, as it inevitably did in 1960, Congo was desperately unprepared to govern itself.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，当独立时刻在1960年不可避免地到来时，刚果对自我治理毫无准备。

sentences.en: There was no political infrastructure, no experienced civil service, no established judiciary, and no military leadership beyond the Belgian officers who had run the Force Publique.
sentences.zh: 这里没有政治基础设施，没有经验丰富的公务员队伍，没有既定的司法系统，除了运营国民军的比利时军官之外，也没有军事领导层。

sentences.en: Unlike British or French colonies, which had at least had some form of elite education system for local people, Belgium had deliberately avoided training a Congolese professional class.
sentences.zh: 不同于英国或法国殖民地至少为当地人提供某种形式的精英教育体系，比利时刻意避免培养刚果的专业阶层。

sentences.en: Indeed, at the time of independence in 1960, there were just 30 Congolese university graduates in the entire country, a country of around 15 million people at the time.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在1960年独立时，整个国家只有30名刚果大学毕业生，而当时这个国家的人口约为1500万。

sentences.en: So, back to Mobutu. At the time of Congolese independence, he had been working as a journalist for a few years, and had become friendly with a man named Patrice Lumumba.
sentences.zh: 所以，回到蒙博托身上。在刚果独立时，他已经当了几年的记者，并与一个名叫帕特里斯·卢蒙巴（Patrice Lumumba）的人成为了朋友。

sentences.en: Lumumba was a fiery orator and committed nationalist who won the country’s first democratic election.
sentences.zh: 卢蒙巴是一位慷慨激昂的演说家和坚定的民族主义者，赢得了该国历史上第一次民主选举。

sentences.en: As his secretary, he chose Mobutu. But if you are thinking of “secretary” as an administrative helper who brought coffee and tea, and greeted guests at the reception, no, Mobutu was a very different kind of secretary.
sentences.zh: 他选择了蒙博托作为他的秘书。但如果你把“秘书”想象成一个端茶倒水、在接待处迎宾的行政助理，那就大错特错了，蒙博托是另一种完全不同的秘书。

sentences.en: He was charismatic, spoke several languages, fiercely intelligent, and was effectively Lumumba’s trusted right hand man and confidant.
sentences.zh: 他极具个人魅力，精通数门语言，聪明绝顶，实际上是卢蒙巴最信任的得力助手和知己。

sentences.en: Or as one US ambassador’s private notes put it, “this was an extremely intelligent man, very young, perhaps immature, but a man with great potential”.
sentences.zh: 或者正如一位美国大使的私人笔记所写的那样，“这是一个极其聪明的人，非常年轻，或许还不成熟，但有着巨大的潜力”。

sentences.en: Lumumba had clearly seen this potential, too, and promoted Mobutu to colonel and soon after, Chief of Staff of the national army - a meteoric rise that gave him enormous influence over the country’s only cohesive institution at the time.
sentences.zh: 卢蒙巴显然也看出了这种潜力，将蒙博托晋升为上校，不久后又任命他为国家军队参谋长——这是一次火箭般的升迁，使他对当时国内唯一的凝聚力机构产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: But for Lumumba it would backfire terribly.
sentences.zh: 但对卢蒙巴来说，这却产生了可怕的反噬。

sentences.en: Shortly after the declaration of independence, on the 30th of June 1960, the country had fallen into disarray.
sentences.zh: 就在1960年6月30日独立宣言发表后不久，国家就陷入了混乱。

sentences.en: Lumumba was technically the Prime Minister, but his hold on the country was shaky at best.
sentences.zh: 卢蒙巴名义上是总理，但他对国家的控制力可以说是岌岌可危。

sentences.en: Force Publique soldiers mutinied, and when it looked like the United Nations peacekeepers sent in to help wouldn’t be able to contain them, the Prime Minister, Lumumba, turned to the Soviet Union for assistance.
sentences.zh: 国民军士兵哗变，当派来协助的联合国维和部队看似无法控制局势时，总理卢蒙巴向苏联寻求了援助。

sentences.en: The Soviets sent technical advisors and support, which helped quell the unrest, but created an altogether different problem.
sentences.zh: 苏联人派遣了技术顾问和支持，这平息了骚乱，却带来了完全不同的问题。

sentences.en: This was 1960, the peak of the Cold War, and the United States got very nervous at the idea of Soviet influence in the newly independent Congo.
sentences.zh: 那是1960年，冷战正酣，美国对苏联在刚果这个新独立国家的影响力感到非常紧张。

sentences.en: With the backing of Belgian and, most likely, also U.S. intelligence, Mobutu orchestrated a coup -like intervention that removed Lumumba from power.
sentences.zh: 在比利时情报机构、且极有可能是美国情报机构的支持下，蒙博托策划了一场类似政变的干预，将卢蒙巴赶下台。

sentences.en: Lumumba fled, was arrested by troops loyal to Mobutu, but instead of being tried or protected, he was flown to a breakaway province hostile to his leadership and handed over to his enemies.
sentences.zh: 卢蒙巴逃跑了，被忠于蒙博托的军队逮捕，但他没有受到审判或保护，而是被空运到一个敌视他领导的分裂省份，并被交给了他的敌人。

sentences.en: There, the country’s first democratically elected leader was brutally tortured and executed, with Belgian officers watching on.
sentences.zh: 在那里，这个国家第一位民选领导人在比利时军官的围观下遭到残酷虐待和处决。

sentences.en: His death shocked the world and remains one of the darkest stains on Congo’s post-independence history.
sentences.zh: 他的死震惊了世界，至今仍是刚果独立后历史中最黑暗的污点之一。

sentences.en: Now, importantly, this first “coup”, as it's been called, was relatively bloodless.
sentences.zh: 需要指出的是，这次被称为“政变”的行动相对来说是流血不多的。

sentences.en: It wasn’t good news if you were Patrice Lumumba, but it seemed like Mobutu was a loyal army officer who only had the best in mind for his country.
sentences.zh: 如果你是帕特里斯·卢蒙巴，这当然不是什么好消息，但当时看起来，蒙博托只是一名忠诚的军官，一心为国家着想。

sentences.en: He claimed it was a “neutralisation” of all political figures, Lumumba included, and declared that Congo would be governed by technocrats for the following six months.
sentences.zh: 他声称这是对包括卢蒙巴在内的所有政治人物的“中立化”，并宣布刚果将在接下来的六个月里由技术官僚治理。

sentences.en: What actually happened, though, was less a smooth technocratic transition and more a chaotic power vacuum.
sentences.zh: 然而，实际发生的情况与其说是一个平稳的技术官僚过渡，不如说是一个混乱的权力真空。

sentences.en: The so-called “neutral government” that Mobutu installed quickly lost legitimacy.
sentences.zh: 蒙博托安插的所谓“中立政府”很快失去了合法性。

sentences.en: Regional leaders and army officers began acting independently.
sentences.zh: 地方领袖和军队将领开始各自为政。

sentences.en: The country effectively fractured. In the mineral-rich south, backed by Belgian mining interests, one province declared independence.
sentences.zh: 国家实际上陷入了分裂。在矿产丰富的南部，在比利时采矿利益集团的支持下，一个省份宣布独立。

sentences.en: In the east, another city became a stronghold for Lumumba’s supporters.
sentences.zh: 在东部，另一个城市成为了卢蒙巴支持者的坚固据点。

sentences.en: There were foreign troops from the United Nations, Belgian commandos, and even Cuban advisors in the mix.
sentences.zh: 其中还夹杂着来自联合国的外国军队、比利时突击队员，甚至还有古巴顾问。

sentences.en: The entire country was being pulled apart by competing forces, and Mobutu, far from being a neutral arbiter, was quietly consolidating power in the background.
sentences.zh: 整个国家被互相竞争的势力四分五裂，而蒙博托非但不是一个中立的仲裁者，反而在幕后悄悄地巩固权力。

sentences.en: Over the next few years, he positioned himself as the one figure who could hold the country together.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几年里，他把自己塑造成唯一能够将国家团结在一起的人物。

sentences.en: And to a population exhausted by years of instability and civil war, the idea of a strongman didn’t sound so bad.
sentences.zh: 对于被多年的动荡和内战搞得身心俱疲的人民来说，“强人”的概念听起来似乎并不是那么坏。

sentences.en: So, in 1965, at the age of 35, Mobutu saw his chance.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1965年，35岁的蒙博托看到了机会。

sentences.en: He used a request from the President to “temporarily restore order” as a springboard to launch a military coup.
sentences.zh: 他利用总统“暂时恢复秩序”的请求作为跳板，发动了一场军事政变。

sentences.en: He seized control of the country, and in a landmark speech, declared that Congo had been so damaged by politicians and bad actors in the five years since independence that it would take at least another five years to get things back on track.
sentences.zh: 他夺取了国家控制权，并在一次划时代的演讲中宣布，自独立以来的五年里，国家已被政客和坏分子破坏得如此严重，以至于需要至少再花五年时间才能让事情回到正轨。

sentences.en: So he dissolved parliament, banned all political parties, and declared that for the next five years, there would only be one voice in the Congo: his.
sentences.zh: 于是他解散了议会，取缔了所有政党，并宣布在接下来的五年里，刚果只能有一个声音：那就是他的声音。

sentences.en: This was 1965, and for the next 32 years, he would rule the country through a mixture of carrot, stick, and cult of personality.
sentences.zh: 那是1965年，在接下来的32年里，他通过胡萝卜加大棒和个人崇拜相结合的方式统治着这个国家。

sentences.en: And so began the process of rebranding not just Mobutu the man, but the nation itself.
sentences.zh: 于是，一场不仅针对蒙博托个人、更是针对整个国家的新包装运动开始了。

sentences.en: In 1971, he renamed the country Zaire, saying the name “Congo” was a relic of colonialism.
sentences.zh: 1971年，他将国家更名为扎伊尔（Zaire），称“刚果”这个名字是殖民主义的残余。

sentences.en: He also renamed himself, dropping “Joseph-Désiré” and adopting a far more theatrical title: Mobutu Sese Seko Kuku Ngbendu wa Za Banga, which roughly translates as “the all-powerful warrior who, because of his endurance and inflexible will to win, goes from conquest to conquest, leaving fire in his wake.”
sentences.zh: 他也给自己改了名字，去掉了“约瑟夫-德西雷”，换上了一个极具戏剧性的头衔：Mobutu Sese Seko Kuku Ngbendu wa Za Banga，大致翻译为“这位全能的战士，由于他的忍耐和不可动摇的获胜意志，从一个征服走向另一个征服，所到之处留下一片火海。”

sentences.en: Quite something. And he didn’t stop there.
sentences.zh: 真是相当惊人。而且他并未就此止步。

sentences.en: Streets, cities, rivers, and even clothing were swept up in this new cultural vision.
sentences.zh: 街道、城市、河流甚至服装都被卷入了这股新的文化愿景中。

sentences.en: Western names were replaced with African ones.
sentences.zh: 西方名字被非洲名字所取代。

sentences.en: Suits and ties were banned from government offices and replaced with a collarless shirt known as the “abacost”, which is short for à bas le costume, or “down with the suit”.
sentences.zh: 西装和领带被政府办公室禁用，取而代之的是一种名为“abacost”的无领衬衫，这是法语 à bas le costume（意为“打倒西装”）的简称。

sentences.en: Foreign music was pushed aside in favour of homegrown styles.
sentences.zh: 外国音乐被推到一旁，取而代之的是本土风格。

sentences.en: The whole campaign was called the Authenticité movement, meaning “authenticity” in English.
sentences.zh: 整场运动被称为“Authenticité”（意为“真实性”）运动。

sentences.en: Now, this movement was initially very popular in the Congo, or Zaire as it was then.
sentences.zh: 最初，这场运动在刚果（当时的扎伊尔）非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: And it was also praised by some foreign commentators.
sentences.zh: 它也受到了一些外国评论员的赞扬。

sentences.en: After all, Mobutu was pushing for a kind of cultural decolonisation, encouraging pride in African identity after decades of European rule.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，蒙博托当时正极力推动某种形式的文化去殖民化，在经历了几年的欧洲统治后，激发人们对非洲身份的自豪感。

sentences.en: But others were more sceptical. They said it was less about pride and more about power.
sentences.zh: 但另一些人则更为怀疑。他们认为这与其说是关于自豪感，不如说是关于权力。

sentences.en: Authenticité didn’t just strip the country of European names; it gave Mobutu the excuse to eliminate anyone who wasn’t “authentically Zairian,” or who disagreed with his vision of what that meant.
sentences.zh: Authenticité 运动不仅剥夺了欧洲名字，还给蒙博托提供了借口，去消灭任何不属于“真正扎伊尔人”或不同意他这一愿景的人。

sentences.en: He was now not just the president, but something closer to a monarch.
sentences.zh: 他现在不仅是总统，更接近于一个君王。

sentences.en: He installed giant portraits of himself in public squares.
sentences.zh: 他在公共广场上树立了自己的巨幅画像。

sentences.en: His face appeared on banknotes, stamps, and schoolbooks.
sentences.zh: 他的脸出现在纸币、邮票和教科书上。

sentences.en: He referred to himself as “the father of the nation,” “the guide,” and “the messiah.” At official events, his name would often be introduced with a list of over a dozen honorific titles.
sentences.zh: 他自称为“国父”、“导师”和“弥赛亚”。在官方活动中，介绍他的名字时往往会附带一长串十几个荣誉头衔。

sentences.en: And of course, there was the leopard-skin hat.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有那顶豹皮帽。

sentences.en: Always present, always perfectly positioned.
sentences.zh: 永远都在，永远戴得完美无缺。

sentences.en: It became a symbol of his rule; part theatre, part menace.
sentences.zh: 它成了他统治的象征；既有戏剧性，又带有一丝威胁。

sentences.en: Alongside it came his carved ebony walking stick, his dark glasses, and his meticulously tailored abacost.
sentences.zh: 与它相伴的还有他的乌木雕刻手杖、墨镜和精心剪裁的 abacost 衬衫。

sentences.en: This was a man who took image seriously, a man who understood the power of performance.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重视形象的男人，一个深谙表演力量的男人。

sentences.en: But behind the smiling portraits and grandiose titles was a deeply repressive regime.
sentences.zh: 但在微笑着的画像和宏大的头衔背后，是一个极其压制异己的政权。

sentences.en: Dissidents were routinely tortured or disappeared, opposition parties were outlawed, and intelligence agencies kept the population under constant surveillance.
sentences.zh: 持不同政见者经常遭到酷刑折磨或人间蒸发，反对党被取缔，情报机构对民众实施无休止的监控。

sentences.en: Public executions were staged to send a message.
sentences.zh: 公开处决被用来杀鸡儆猴。

sentences.en: Mobutu’s grip on power wasn’t just psychological; it was brutally enforced.
sentences.zh: 蒙博托对权力的掌控不仅仅停留在心理层面，而是靠残酷的手段强力推行。

sentences.en: And during all of this, the country was in a serious state of decay.
sentences.zh: 正是在这一切发生的同时，国家却在严重腐烂。

sentences.en: Mobutu ruled through a complex web of patronage, of dispersing power, favours and money to his family, friends and allies.
sentences.zh: 蒙博托通过复杂的裙带关系网络进行统治，将权力、恩惠和金钱分发给他的家人、朋友和盟友。

sentences.en: If you were loyal, you were rewarded. If you weren’t, you were either exiled, imprisoned, or worse.
sentences.zh: 如果你忠诚，你就会得到奖励。如果你不忠，你就会被流放、监禁，甚至更惨。

sentences.en: Corruption wasn’t just tolerated, it was built into the system.
sentences.zh: 腐败不仅被容忍，而且被嵌入了体制之中。

sentences.en: In one speech, he said, “If you want to steal, steal a little in a nice way.
sentences.zh: 在一次演讲中，他说：“如果你想偷窃，那就温和地偷一点。”

sentences.en: Only if you steal so much as to become rich overnight, you will be caught.”
sentences.zh: “只有当你偷得太多以至于一夜暴富时，你才会被抓。”

sentences.en: Perhaps he should have clarified that there was one man for whom this rule didn’t apply: him.
sentences.zh: 也许他本该澄清，有一个人是这个规则不适用的：那就是他自己。

sentences.en: Estimates vary, but Mobutu is believed to have embezzled somewhere between $4 and $15 billion during his time in power.
sentences.zh: 据估计，蒙博托在当权期间贪污了40亿到150亿美元不等。

sentences.en: Indeed, in 1970, he is estimated to have stolen 60% of the entire country’s annual budget.
sentences.zh: 事实上，据估计，仅在1970年他就盗用了全国年度预算的60%。

sentences.en: And this wasn’t all stashed away in Swiss bank accounts; there were lavish displays of wealth and opulence.
sentences.zh: 这些钱并非全都藏在瑞士银行的账户里，他还大肆炫耀财富和奢华。

sentences.en: He built a huge palace in his ancestral home in northern Congo, which was dubbed “The Versailles of the Jungle”.
sentences.zh: 他在刚果北部的祖籍地建造了一座巨大的宫殿，被称为“丛林凡尔赛”。

sentences.en: He had more homes in France, Portugal, and Switzerland.
sentences.zh: 他在法国、葡萄牙和瑞士拥有更多豪宅。

sentences.en: He travelled with a refrigerated case of pink champagne, and there are reports of suits being sent to Paris for dry cleaning.
sentences.zh: 他出行时带着装满粉红香槟的冷藏箱，据报道还有人把西装送到巴黎干洗。

sentences.en: In the 1980s, he even reportedly had a Concorde jet pick him up for shopping trips in Europe.
sentences.zh: 上世纪80年代，据传他甚至曾用协和飞机接送自己去欧洲购物。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, back in Zaire, as it was then, schools crumbled, hospitals lacked medicine, teachers and civil servants often went unpaid for months.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在当时的扎伊尔，学校倒塌，医院缺乏药品，教师和公务员常常几个月拿不到工资。

sentences.en: The economy became increasingly dependent on foreign aid and loans.
sentences.zh: 经济越来越依赖外国援助和贷款。

sentences.en: And when there was a crash in the price of copper, which was one of Zaire’s main exports, the country literally ran out of money.
sentences.zh: 当作为扎伊尔主要出口产品之一的铜价暴跌时，国家简直陷入了山穷水尽的地步。

sentences.en: Inflation soared, debt piled up, and the state became little more than an empty shell.
sentences.zh: 通货膨胀飙升，债务堆积如山，国家沦空壳一个。

sentences.en: Yet, Mobutu remained in power. Partly because he was a master manipulator, but also because of geopolitics.
sentences.zh: 然而，蒙博托依然稳坐江山。部分原因是他是一个操纵大师，但也归功于地缘政治。

sentences.en: Throughout the Cold War, the West had seen him as a reliable anti-communist ally.
sentences.zh: 在整个冷战期间，西方一直视他为可靠的反共盟友。

sentences.en: He hosted CIA operations, supported US-backed rebels in Angola, and regularly reminded Washington that if they didn’t support him, the Soviets might take over.
sentences.zh: 他接待中央情报局的行动，支持美国在安哥拉的叛军，并经常提醒华盛顿，如果他们不支持他，苏联可能会接管。

sentences.en: The irony, of course, was that Mobutu wasn’t exactly consistent in his ideology.
sentences.zh: 当然，具有讽刺意味的是，蒙博托的意识形态其实并不那么一致。

sentences.en: He had been outspoken in his admiration for Mao Zedong, and had flirted with ideas from the Chinese Revolution.
sentences.zh: 他曾公开表达对毛泽东的崇拜，并对中国革命的思想产生过兴趣。

sentences.en: He condemned European decadence all while sipping French champagne and collecting fine European art.
sentences.zh: 他一边品尝着法国香槟、收藏着欧洲艺术品，一边谴责欧洲的腐朽。

sentences.en: He presented himself as the symbol of African pride, while secretly collaborating with Belgian intelligence to remove Lumumba, one of the continent’s great anti-colonial leaders.
sentences.zh: 他把自己塑造成非洲自豪感的象征，暗地里却与比利时情报机构合作除掉了卢蒙巴这位非洲大陆伟大的反殖民领袖。

sentences.en: It was hard to see what he stood for, apart from his personal enrichment, that was.
sentences.zh: 除了他个人的发家致富之外，很难看出他到底代表了什么。

sentences.en: And by the early 1990s, things were falling apart.
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪90年代初，一切都开始瓦解。

sentences.en: The Cold War was over, and as there was no threat of the Soviet Union trying to push communist ideology in Africa, the West no longer needed Mobutu.
sentences.zh: 冷战已经结束，由于苏联不再试图在非洲推行共产主义意识形态，西方不再需要蒙博托了。

sentences.en: The Aid dried up. Western diplomats, who had once been his staunch allies, now publicly called for democratic reform.
sentences.zh: 援助枯竭了。曾经是他坚定盟友的西方外交官现在公开呼吁进行民主改革。

sentences.en: And inside the country, people were fed up.
sentences.zh: 国内的人民也已经忍无可忍。

sentences.en: Civil servants hadn’t been paid in months.
sentences.zh: 公务员已经几个月没有领到工资了。

sentences.en: University students were protesting. The army was unpaid and increasingly mutinous.
sentences.zh: 大学生们在抗议。军队拿不到军饷，哗变情绪日益高涨。

sentences.en: Strikes, demonstrations, and riots became common.
sentences.zh: 罢工、游行和暴动变得屡见不鲜。

sentences.en: The myth of Mobutu’s invincibility began to crumble, and with it, the carefully constructed image of the “father of the nation.”
sentences.zh: 蒙博托战无不胜的神话开始破灭，随之破灭的还有他精心构建的“国父”形象。

sentences.en: Pro-democracy movements were sweeping the continent.
sentences.zh: 民主运动席卷整个非洲大陆。

sentences.en: Mobutu, who was now ageing and increasingly unwell, was forced to start promising reforms.
sentences.zh: 年事已高且健康状况每况愈下的蒙博托被迫开始承诺改革。

sentences.en: He said there would be free elections. But they never came.
sentences.zh: 他说会有自由选举。但选举从未兑现。

sentences.en: In 1996, a rebellion sprung up across the country.
sentences.zh: 1996年，全国各地爆发了叛乱。

sentences.en: Their armies swept through eastern Zaire with lightning speed, facing little resistance.
sentences.zh: 他们的军队以闪电般的速度横扫扎伊尔东部，几乎没有遇到什么抵抗。

sentences.en: Mobutu’s once-feared army barely fought back.
sentences.zh: 蒙博托曾经令人闻风丧胆的军队几乎没有进行抵抗。

sentences.en: Many soldiers simply deserted, while others joined the rebellion.
sentences.zh: 许多士兵直接开小差，其他人则加入了叛军。

sentences.en: In a matter of months, the rebels had captured vast swathes of the country.
sentences.zh: 短短几个月内，叛军就攻占了大片国土。

sentences.en: Their leader, a man named Laurent-Désiré Kabila, promised an end to dictatorship, and as his forces advanced westward, city after city fell without a fight.
sentences.zh: 他们的领袖洛朗-德西雷·卡比拉（Laurent-Désiré Kabila）承诺结束独裁统治，随着他的部队向西推进，一座又一座城市不战而降。

sentences.en: Mobutu’s control evaporated almost overnight.
sentences.zh: 蒙博托的控制力几乎在一夜之间蒸发了。

sentences.en: So, he fled. First to his palace in the north of the country, the so-called Versailles of the Jungle.
sentences.zh: 于是，他逃跑了。首先逃到了他位于国家北部的宫殿，也就是所谓的“丛林凡尔赛”。

sentences.en: He attempted to negotiate a peace deal, but no one was interested.
sentences.zh: 他试图通过谈判达成和平协议，但根本无人理睬。

sentences.en: The world had moved on. What’s more, he was a very sick man, and had been battling prostate cancer.
sentences.zh: 世界已经向前看了。更何况，他是一个病入膏肓的人，一直在与前列腺癌作斗争。

sentences.en: He tried to negotiate with France for medical treatment, but they refused.
sentences.zh: 他试图与法国协商医疗救治，但遭到拒绝。

sentences.en: No one wanted to be seen propping him up anymore.
sentences.zh: 没有人再想被人看到在背后支撑他了。

sentences.en: He boarded a plane and flew to Togo, then to Morocco, where he had property.
sentences.zh: 他登上一架飞机飞往多哥，然后前往他拥有房产的摩洛哥。

sentences.en: He arrived in Rabat as a disgraced former leader, his entourage vastly reduced, his fortune frozen or looted.
sentences.zh: 他以一个失势的前领导人身份抵达拉巴特，随行人员寥寥无几，财富被冻结或遭洗劫。

sentences.en: He died just a few months later, in September 1997, aged 66.
sentences.zh: 几个月后，即1997年9月，他在66岁时去世。

sentences.en: There was no state funeral, no national mourning.
sentences.zh: 没有国葬，也没有全国哀悼。

sentences.en: Just a quiet death in a foreign land, a dramatic fall for a man who had once styled himself as the embodiment of a nation.
sentences.zh: 只有在异国他乡的静悄悄的死亡，对于一个曾把自己塑造成国家化身的男人来说，这是一个戏剧性的陨落。

sentences.en: And yet, his legacy lives on. Not in statues or street names–most of those were removed a long time ago–but in the structure of the state he left behind.
sentences.zh: 然而，他的政治遗产依然存在。不是以雕像或街名的形式——那些早就被移除了——而是留在他所建立的国家体制中。

sentences.en: A system of patronage, of centralised power, of wealth concentrated in the hands of a few.
sentences.zh: 一种裙带关系、权力高度集中、财富集中在少数人手中的体制。

sentences.en: The Democratic Republic of Congo is one of the wealthiest countries in the world in terms of its natural resources, with huge deposits of copper, cobalt, gold, diamonds, and other precious metals.
sentences.zh: 就自然资源而言，刚果民主共和国是世界上最富有的国家之一，拥有巨额的铜、钴、金、钻石和其他贵金属储量。

sentences.en: It has a population of more than 100 million people, yet 75% of them live in poverty.
sentences.zh: 它拥有超过1亿的人口，然而其中75%的人生活在贫困之中。

sentences.en: In 1960, when Mobutu first took power, it was one of the most industrialised countries in Africa, second only to South Africa.
sentences.zh: 1960年蒙博托刚上掌权时，它是非洲工业化程度最高的国家之一，仅次于南非。

sentences.en: It is now one of the poorest. Clearly, there are many more reasons for this than Mobutu Sese Seko.
sentences.zh: 而如今它成了最贫穷的国家之一。显然，造成这一现状的原因远不止 Mobutu Sese Seko 一个人。

sentences.en: He was a man of his time. A product of colonialism, Cold War politics, and personal ambition.
sentences.zh: 他是特定时代的产物。是殖民主义、冷战政治和个人野心的结晶。

sentences.en: But his story is also a warning, of what happens when power is unchecked, when image replaces substance, and when a country is ruled not for its people, but for the enrichment of a single man in a leopard-skin hat.
sentences.zh: 但他的故事也是一个警示：当权力失去制衡、当形式替代实质、当一个国家不是为人民统治，而是为了一个戴着豹皮帽的男人的个人暴富时，会发生什么。

sentences.en: OK then, that is it for today's episode on Mobutu Sese Seko, or to give him his full title, “the all-powerful warrior who, because of his endurance and inflexible will to win, goes from conquest to conquest, leaving fire in his wake.”
sentences.zh: 好了，这就是今天关于 Mobutu Sese Seko（或者用他的全名：“这位全能的战士，由于他的忍耐和不可动摇的获胜意志，从一个征服走向另一个征服，所到之处留下一片火海”）的节目的全部内容。

sentences.en: As a quick reminder, this is part one of a three-part mini-series on the loose theme of power struggles in post-colonial Africa.
sentences.zh: 简单提醒一下，这是关于后殖民非洲权力斗争这一宽泛主题的三集迷你系列的第一部分。

sentences.en: Next up, in part two, will be an episode on Simon Mann, the ex-Etonian who tried to hatch a plot to launch a coup in Equatorial Guinea.
sentences.zh: 接下来，在第二部分中，将有一集关于 Simon Mann 的节目，这位前伊顿公学学生曾企图在赤道几内亚发动政变。

sentences.en: And in part three, we will be talking about the Angolan Model, and the new economic model China is pioneering on the continent.
sentences.zh: 在第三部分中，我们将讨论“安哥拉模式”，以及中国正在非洲大陆开创的全新经济模式。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，请注意安全，我们下期节目见。
